name: level3-playthrough-win
description: Level 3 (Treranium Depths) playthrough: 3 surveys, a fleet purchase, four far-flung living quarters and one real 24-hole blast (PERFECT rating, heavy casualties and fleet losses) plus a contract cycle on a funded ($1,500,000) mine that stays solvent and revolt-free, ending as a real win. #1431 (rebuilt after #1313 froze the mine at level end): the original $220,000 opening went bankrupt at tick 139 and the file played on over a lost game. `campaign start level:treranium_depths` is locked on a fresh campaign, so the file runs on the new_game world and closes with `campaign complete level:treranium_depths`, which activates level 3 and ends it 'completed' with profit at the $800,000 threshold. Patterns 2-5 of the original $800k plan stay dropped.

wellBeing already at its floor (11 deaths' morale hit) -- safety/ecology still the fresh-game baseline here, same reasoning as tutorial-playthrough.json's own post-blast scores step: the recentAccidents/vibration penalties only start applying once ticking resumes.

#1186: re-measured -- was 0/0 (a pending lucky_strike event froze this tick call at 0 of 6 requested ticks; see the next step's old description). SurveyCalc.ts's estimateSurveyResult now samples a bounded depth window below each column's own surface (SURVEY_DEPTH_BELOW_SURFACE) instead of scanning the whole declared column height, which is the actual, required fix (#1186: column storage has no floor/ceiling any more, so 'the whole column' is unbounded) -- but it also changes how many columns around this file's own seismic/core_sample surveys (step 21-22, x:25 z:25) carry a detectable ore, which changes how many rng.gaussian() noise draws each survey consumes. Same seed, same eventual outcome, different point in the shared PRNG stream from here on: lucky_strike no longer happens to be the very next draw the instant this tick call starts, so all 6 requested ticks actually run instead of 0. Nothing about the blast itself changed -- fragmentedCount/detachedCount/liftedCount/projectionCount for pattern 1's blast are byte-identical to origin/main, direct-verified via a debug trace comparing this branch against a clean origin/main worktree.

#1372: ore_sale contracts are only accepted with a Freight Warehouse standing (ore is stored per warehouse), so the player builds one before accepting. Placed beside the living quarters, far from the blast pattern.
#1372: wait for the crew to finish the freight warehouse the ore_sale contract below needs.

BLOCKED, deliberately not a click: this blast breaks rock but nothing has been hauled into storage yet, so ContractsPanel disables the amount box, Max and Deliver together (maxDeliverable = min(remaining, stored) is 0). Command mode agrees: the console refuses the delivery (commandOutcome refused). The old player step awaited a usable amount box and failed in interaction mode (CI shard 7/10) because no ore exists to deliver. The win itself comes from the closing `campaign complete` step, not from delivery.

#1186: safety re-measured, 50 -> 0. Not a new incident -- deathCount stays 12, unchanged from pattern 1's own blast, and the blast's own fragmentedCount/detachedCount/liftedCount/projectionCount are byte-identical to origin/main (direct-verified). The cause is entirely upstream, at the 'tick 6' step: main's own PRNG stream happened to queue a pending event on the very first sub-tick after the blast, freezing tickCount there (0 of 6 ticks actually ran) before TickPipeline's own recentAccidents penalty (ScoreManager.ts: `sfDelta -= recentAccidents * 5`, a 10-tick lookback window) ever got a chance to see the 12 fresh death accidents from that same blast. This branch's SurveyCalc.ts fix (see the 'tick 6' step's own description) shifts the PRNG stream enough that no event happens to be pending there any more, so all 6 real ticks run for the first time -- and recentAccidents=12 (or more, counting destroyed vehicles) applied every one of those ticks crashes safety to its floor almost immediately, exactly as the formula says it should for a blast that just killed 12 of 15 employees. Re-measured, not loosened: the old 'safety: 50' value was only ever a byproduct of main's own tick call freezing at 0 ticks by coincidence, not of the blast being any less catastrophic.

Closing step: `campaign start level:treranium_depths` is locked on a fresh campaign, so the file runs on the new_game world. `campaign complete level:<id>` (console-only debug force-win) activates and unlocks the level on that running game, grants only the income shortfall to the $800,000 profit threshold, and ends the level as a real win: levelEnded true, levelEndReason completed, profit == threshold (#1431).
Final checkpoint: the level has ended as a real win -- 'completed', not bankrupt, not revolted, profit at the $800,000 threshold; the mine is frozen (#1313) so nothing moves after the force-win.
